what_to_detect: A resolution asks a player to draw more cards than their library holds: the player draws what is left (card_drawn short of the requested number, the snapshot's library count below it) and loses the game in the next state-based check, the game-outcome record right after it naming another player in player_won.
near_miss: A draw resolution whose requested number the library covers: every draw finds a card and the player stays in the game.
record_fields: player_won, which BusBracketCollector.flushOrphanedEvents files in a record of its own after the resolution, with no ability, never in the Draw resolution's effect half

what_to_detect: A resolution after whose own life changes or damage every player still in the game is at 0 or less life (or every one meets a loss condition at once), and no player_won follows: the game is a draw.
near_miss: A resolution that takes at least one player to 0 or less while another stays above 0, who then wins.
record_fields: life_change and damage_dealt events per player
absence of player_won (not filed on a draw) in the record and the orphan record after it

what_to_detect: A resolution in which a segment whose script API is GameDrawn had its condition met and ran, ending the game as a draw. Every GameDrawn in the card pool is a conditional sub-ability, so the acting line's root API never names it, and game_drawn has no emitter.
near_miss: A resolution of the same chain whose GameDrawn segment's condition was not met: the game goes on.
record_fields: the sidecar's script chain, segment API types
absence of player_won (not filed on a draw)
